prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather(padded bus/loader/tow; RFM may raise stand absorption vs unstable taxi queues); Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor agree metering-horizon extension so delay absorbed pre-pushback); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved shorter cycles, no pushback surges); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance; Winter operating mode(Regional Flow Platform enters on freezing precip/contamination/low surface temp; Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms triggers in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity for deicing/pad transit/slow taxi; Airport Capacity Plan gets winter margin before Blueharbor recalculates CTTs). Actors: Regional Flow Manager, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Tower Supervisor, Airport Duty Manager, Ramp Control Lead(reviews pushback windows), Aircraft Operator Representative(requests stand-delay reconsideration via Foxglove), Airline Operations Coordinator(confirms stand-delay absorbability), Deicing Coordinator(pad config: bays, fluid, vehicles), Meteorology Briefing Officer; Halcyon logs pushback rationale. Regional Flow Platform=Cedarbell: normalizes Flight Intent Message vs Airport Capacity Plan; proposes TOBT, locks at freeze horizon; separates ATC/handling delay. Parts: Demand Prediction Service=Marlinstone; Capacity Assessment Module(demand vs AAR, runway config; Orchard weather input); Slot Allocation Engine=Blueharbor(CTT; priority emergency/national>scheduled>GA); Airport CDM Portal=Foxglove; Departure Metering Service=Emberline(TOBT protecting CTT; stand absorption; CTT→Tower Sequence Manager=Ironleaf); Business Rules Registry(max runway queue, warning, intervention thresholds per runway config); Alert Distribution Hub(highlights queue >warning on Common Situation Display); Gate Conflict Detector(warns stand hold blocks inbound/equipment move); Pad queue controls(assign deicing lane only when TOBT stable); North/South Runway Meter; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensor; Ramp Movement Board=Skylark(Fuel Truck Hold Advice; states pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, returning to stand); Weather Ingest Gateway=Orchard; Flight Data Exchange; Airline Interface Adapter; Time Synchronization Service; Performance Analytics Warehouse(verifies planned absorption, AOBT, queue vs thresholds); Collaborative Decision

New part:
S378: Ramp Control Lead uses the queue card to verify pad entry order before authorizing a movement from the staging area.
S379: When demand exceeds the safe holding capacity near the pad, the Departure Metering Service withholds further push clearances until the pad queue falls below the configured threshold.
S380: The Tower Sequence Manager reserves departure sequence positions only for aircraft with an achievable pad release time and a valid runway taxi path.
S381: The Airport CDM Portal records the selected fluid type, mixture ratio, treatment start time, treatment completion time, and expected holdover reference for each treated aircraft.
S382: Fluid status updates are timestamped through the Time Synchronization Service so that ramp, tower, and airline users interpret treatment age consistently.
S383: The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates remaining fluid inventory and truck serviceability when replenishment, contamination, or equipment faults affect the planned treatment rate.
S384: The Handling Resource Planner compares fluid inventory with scheduled deicing demand and warns when a planned bank cannot be supported without resequencing.
S385: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews aircraft readiness and may request a later pad entry when crew, catering, or passenger status would cause holdover time to be wasted.
S386: Gate Conflict Detector produces the Gate Reopening Memo when a stand becomes usable after snow clearance and the gate occupancy constraint has been removed.
S387: Quartzline must coordinate every pad release with the Tower Supervisor before the aircraft leaves the treated area.
S388: Under freezing conditions, the Tower Supervisor protects runway departure spacing by accounting for reduced braking action, slower lineup, and possible repeat treatment requests.
S389: The Surface Surveillance Adapter confirms that aircraft leaving the pad follow the assigned route and do not block inbound traffic to the same treatment complex.
S390: If a treated aircraft cannot depart within its applicable holdover reference, the Deicing Coordinator marks the treatment as expired and returns the aircraft to the appropriate queue state.
S391: The Common Situation Display highlights expired treatments, pad closures, fluid shortages, and ramp blockages so that participants can resolve conflicts without separate status calls.
S392: The Collaborative Decision Log captures winter-mode decisions, including capacity changes, pad flow restrictions, and agreed deviations from the normal departure order.
S393: When conditions improve, the Regional Flow Manager authorizes a controlled transition from Capacity Reduction State toward Recovery Phase after pad backlog, runway condition, and surface flow indicators are stable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
